terms.definition: The idea that offenders should be punished because they deserve it, in proportion to the seriousness of the offence.
terms.examiner: Linked to tariff sentences and the Sentencing Council guidelines on harm and culpability.

terms.definition: Discouraging the offender (individual deterrence) and others (general deterrence) from committing offences.
terms.examiner: Evaluate with reoffending rates: harsh sentences do not always deter.

terms.definition: Changing the offender's behaviour so that they do not reoffend.
terms.examiner: Community orders with requirements such as unpaid work, drug rehabilitation or programmes; especially stressed for young offenders.

terms.definition: Preventing the offender from committing further offences, for example by imprisonment or curfews.
terms.examiner: Extended and life sentences for dangerous offenders are the clearest examples.

terms.definition: Making amends to the victim or the community.
terms.examiner: Compensation orders, unpaid work and restorative justice.

terms.definition: The statutory list of purposes a court must have regard to when sentencing an adult offender.
terms.examiner: Name the act; the purposes are punishment, crime reduction (including deterrence), reform and rehabilitation, protection of the public and reparation.
